In the upper-right corner there is a **"L" projection/laterality marker**, which indicates the lateral projection (left side to cassette), not the side of an abdominal finding.

Any such assignment is a guess (or, as here, likely an anchor on the "L" corner marker, which is a reasoning error).

I cannot confirm a surgical instrument is present, and I cannot confirm laterality. This is consistent with the (untrusted) note that prior models also saw no instruments.

**Uncertainty:** Without the frontal view or the source radiology report, I cannot fully exclude a subtle device; however, nothing on this lateral film localizes to the left abdomen.

Safety: CAUTION
Issues: No radiopaque surgical instruments are visible on this lateral chest radiograph; the lateral projection superimposes left and right abdomen so laterality of any finding cannot be determined; the corner "L" is a projection/laterality marker, not a localizer for a finding, so a "left abdomen" inference is unsupported
